about: Which authentic dictionary glyphs Dongba World stages, by role. Every id points to an unaltered glyph extracted from the user's photographed dictionary. Arranging several glyph standees together in a scene (e.g. 火 + 柴 + 燃烧 around the bonfire) is staging, not a new character.

gaps.handling: staged as one 火 glyph standing on two 柴 glyphs; the flame sway, smoke and sparks are animation effects, not glyphs
dancers use the 跳舞 glyph and move round the fire; 围绕 and 围绕相对环绕 mark the gathering and the circle
shown as 说 (speak) followed by 打架 (fight)

gaps.need: 院子 yard, 墙 wall, 篱笆 fence
gaps.handling: yards are plain paper ground shapes, scenery rather than text
小水 (small water) drifts along the stream; 水 and 大江 stand on the banks
the far range is plain colour-block paper ridges, not glyphs; the near mountains are the real 雪山 / 高山 / 山 glyphs
walking and running are an animated adaptation of 人 / 立 / 女人 / 小孩: the glyph is cut at the hip and the two leg pieces swing; the ink shapes are not redrawn

gaps.need: 地形 terrain, water surface, foam
gaps.handling: the rolling ground, stream water and foam are painted scenery, not glyphs
the dictionary gives each ingredient and dish glyph and its meaning; which ingredients make which dish is a game rule, not something the dictionary says
tiny isolated dust specks next to a few glyphs (e.g. beside 杨柳树) are left out of the 3D standees; the glyph cards still show the extraction unchanged
the cut-out for this entry captured the printed Chinese label instead of the glyph, so it is left out of stargazing; the other 明亮 glyph (P2775-3-02) is shown
a win is shown as 攻破村寨 (sack the stronghold), then 捆绑 (bind) and 得到 (obtain); 战败 (defeat) is the only defeat glyph
the lanterns are the glyph 意为在水上点火，火亦燃烧 (lighting a fire on water and it still burns); the dictionary does not call it a river lantern
